clue.text: A five were troubled but helped

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
to have ailed is to have been troubled or unwell

explanation.surface: A small group were in difficulties yet still lent a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan of the old newspaper page gave 'few'; the wordplay needs 'five', the Roman V.
explanation.definitionFit: To have availed someone is to have been of use or service to them.

clue.text: Articles on writing music

parts.note: an is the indefinite article in English grammar
the is the definite article in English grammar
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Grammatical articles are placed on top of a musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the articles above the writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthems are pieces of choral or national music, so the plural fits a general word for musical works.

clue.text: A mature though skittish dilettante

indicators.note: skittish means playful and jumpy, so the letters of the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone grown-up yet frivolous is only a dabbler.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in an art or subject without professional commitment, just like a hobbyist.

clue.text: Beer and some company is all a German wants

indicators.note: some of says only part of the following words is wanted, a run of their letters

explanation.surface: A drink and good company are all that a German asks for.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the second L of 'all' and ends inside 'German'; 'company is' and 'wants' are padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light, bottom-fermented kind of beer.

clue.text: Withdrawing approval? That might be politic

definitions.meaning: read as ..., taking away one's signature of assent
politic can mean shrewd and scheming, crafty in pursuit of one's ends

explanation.definitionFit: De-signing undoes an endorsement, while a designing person is artful and calculating.

clue.text: Am pilot round this ship

indicators.note: round says the steering word goes around the word Am

parts.note: to pilot a vessel is to steer it

explanation.surface: The captain declares that he is guiding this vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a vessel driven by steam power.

clue.text: Support a proud movement

definitions.meaning: a brace or prop in a framework
a swaggering, conceited way of walking

explanation.definitionFit: A strut is both a structural prop and a pompous swaggering gait.

clue.text: Edward's replacing dunderhead with a good man as per direction

indicators.note: replacing says one part of the name is swapped out for something else

parts.note: the name with its possessive s, taken as written
the head of the word dunder is its first letter D
ST, saint, is the crossword's good man

explanation.surface: Edward's sacking a dolt and appointing a virtuous chap, as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' looks like a blockhead but means the head of 'dunder': D in EDWARDS gives way to A plus ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastwards names a heading toward the sunrise, so it describes how something goes in compass terms.

clue.text: Island that's organised a militant body

parts.note: to have organised something is to have made it happen
the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, was a paramilitary group

explanation.surface: An island set up as a paramilitary organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a Portuguese island in the Atlantic, off north-west Africa.

clue.text: A feature for which there's high regard

definitions.meaning: an aspect or detail, as in 'in every way'

explanation.definitionFit: A respect can be a particular point or detail, and respect is also esteem.

clue.text: This could be great as a controller

indicators.note: could be says the words before it may become something else, so their letters rearrange

explanation.surface: Something presented as a possible means of keeping order.
explanation.walkthrough: The controller is crowd control: police use the irritant to disperse riots.
explanation.definitionFit: Tear gas is used by police for riot control, dispersing crowds.

clue.text: Stays concerned with more than one team

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
sides are teams in a game, plural here

explanation.surface: A player remains involved with several teams.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to live or remain in a place, as a stay does.

clue.text: It's a bloomer to look over smart

parts.note: to eye something is to look it over
bright means clever or smart

explanation.surface: Admitting a blunder when checking how clever something is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake; it is a flowering plant, something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small wild flowering plant once used for eye ailments.

clue.text: Pallid after a bit, note

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in 'not a whit'
E is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: Looking pale after a little while, someone takes note.
explanation.definitionFit: White describes a face drained of colour, just as pallid does.

clue.text: Bush given brush-off?

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bush that has been given the cold shoulder?
explanation.walkthrough: 'brush-off' looks like a snub; split it, and 'off' scrambles BRUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a woody plant smaller than a tree, with several stems, the same thing as a bush.

clue.text: Royal insignia displayed in a club restaurant

indicators.note: displayed in says the royal letters are shown inside the club word

parts.note: a brassie is an old name for a golf club, a two wood
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher seen on postboxes

explanation.surface: Royal emblems are put on show in a smart club's dining room.
explanation.walkthrough: The club is a golf club, not a social one: a BRASSIE is an old wooden golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style eating place serving simple dishes.

clue.text: Fit and industrious worker-a teller

parts.note: in form means fit and performing well
the ant is a proverbially hard-working insect

explanation.surface: A healthy and diligent employee working as a bank cashier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teller' suggests a bank clerk; here it is someone who tells, passing on secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: An informant tells the authorities things, so is a teller of secrets.

clue.text: Seem for an alternative for such a member of society

indicators.note: an alternative is another version, so the letters of the words before it take a new order

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to find another arrangement for a certain kind of club member.
explanation.walkthrough: The society is the secret fraternity of Masons.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freemason is a member of the fraternal society of Freemasonry.

clue.text: The figure offered by imprisoned crook

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut in or confined
a crook is a bend, and an angle is a bend or corner

explanation.surface: The number given by a jailed criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal, but it is a bend, as in the crook of the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentangle is a five-pointed star, a geometric figure.

clue.text: The leaf-insect can present quite a spectacle

parts.note: a leaf of a book is a page
the ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A leaf insect can put on quite a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaf-insect' reads as one creature but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is an elaborate public show or procession.

clue.text: Tore up class report

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word goes upward, read backwards

parts.note: tore means rushed, ran
rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A pupil rips up a school report.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to give an account, to report events.

clue.text: A little separately-classed umbelliferous plant

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small plant of the parsley family classified on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedum is a genus of succulent plants, the stonecrops.

clue.text: The cheat swindled five hundred and fifty with little hesitation

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them, so did means swindled
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
er is a short hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A con man stammeringly made off with five hundred and fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: A diddler is a swindler, one who cheats people out of money.

clue.text: Wanting to ruin it, a sovereign married

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
taken as written
a sovereign was a gold pound coin, and L stands for pound

explanation.surface: Someone out to wreck it weds a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is an old British gold coin worth one pound, hence L.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital means relating to marriage, a wedded state.

clue.text: Women soldiers set about right and left

indicators.note: set about says the soldiers are placed around the other letters

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Female troops attack on both flanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Girls is an informal term for young women.

clue.text: Prompter to encompass a balance

indicators.note: to encompass means to surround, so the prompting word goes around the next letter

parts.note: a reminder prompts the memory

explanation.surface: A theatre prompter surrounding a balance.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan printed '8' where the wordplay needs 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the balance outstanding.

clue.text: Continue to strike a man

parts.note: to ram is to strike hard
on means continuing, as in 'carry on'

explanation.surface: Keep on hitting a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramon is a Spanish man's first name.

clue.text: Mixing paint may well be awkward

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Blending paint can be clumsy work.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or clumsy, out of place.

clue.text: A couple of beasts-mixed-up characters

parts.note: a nag is a horse, a beast
a ram is a male sheep, another beast

explanation.surface: Two animals that are confused creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple of' says two beasts are wanted: a horse and a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearrangement of letters is jumbled lettering, characters shuffled.

clue.text: Inebriate going all round the room to find some sort of food

indicators.note: going all round says the drunkard word surrounds the room word

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard, an inebriate
a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: A drunk staggers around the room looking for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion-like bulb used in cooking.

clue.text: The governor joined in it

parts.note: a rein governs or controls a horse

explanation.surface: The ruler took part in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'governor' looks like a ruler, but it is anything that controls: a rein.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is an old-fashioned adverb for inside that place or thing.

clue.text: Taking a turn quite wrongly, a trainee could appear unaffected

indicators.note: quite wrongly says the words before it are put together incorrectly, so rearranged

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A novice going the wrong way could seem unpretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite wrongly' rearranges A TURN as NATUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural means unaffected, behaving without pretence.
